sentences.text: Hard times often teach us lessons that easy times never could.
Some people argue that we learn our most valuable lessons from struggling with our limitations rather than from enjoying our successes.
I largely agree that struggle teaches deeply, but I believe our successes also offer valuable lessons.
First, struggling with our limitations often teaches our deepest lessons.
Failure forces us to look honestly at our weaknesses and find ways to improve.
For example, a student who fails an exam may finally learn how to study properly.
This shows that hardship can teach lessons that comfort and ease never deliver.
Struggle also builds patience, courage, and the strength to keep going.
People who overcome real difficulty often understand themselves far better afterward.
To this extent, our limitations can be powerful teachers.
Second, however, our successes also teach valuable lessons of their own.
Success shows us what we do well and encourages us to build on our strengths.
Consider an athlete who wins a race and learns exactly which training methods truly work.
Such victories teach lessons about what to repeat, not only what to fix.
Enjoying success also builds the confidence that makes future effort possible.
A life of nothing but struggle could leave a person discouraged rather than wise.
Success and struggle, then, both have important lessons to teach.
In conclusion, struggling with our limitations often teaches our deepest and most valuable lessons.
But our successes teach us too, showing us our strengths and building our confidence.
We learn best from both our struggles and our successes, not from either one alone.
